title: How Tibo approaches SaaS acquisition: building trust, due diligence, and making an offer
summary: Tibo's playbook for buying SaaS products: open with a genuine compliment, ask easy questions, state buying intent, and follow up patiently. He then covers technical, financial, legal and marketing due diligence, plus tips like creative deal structuring and verifying Stripe data.

principles.text: Start acquisition talks with a genuine compliment to build trust, not threat.
principles.quote: You are not trying to bring the product down or behaving like a shark to acquire the business. You are genuinely impressed by the product and you are taking time to convey how you like it.

principles.text: Begin with easy, low-effort questions; founders love talking about what they built.
principles.quote: Start by asking questions that are easy to answer and require low effort to respond. So don’t ask for full stats/analysis right away.

principles.text: Treat an initial 'No' as normal; stay friendly and follow up without being pushy.
principles.quote: Even if the answer is No, I maintain a friendly relationship and keep the door open for future interactions.

principles.text: Timing matters: founders are more willing to sell when things start going south.
principles.quote: When the product is newly launched or is doing very well, the founders are enjoying and may refuse to sell. But when things start to go south, founders tend to get more willing to talk about selling.

principles.text: Verify financials directly: require Stripe view-only access and spot-check customer billing.
principles.quote: Get access to their Stripe account (this is a deal break for me if they don’t share view-only access).

principles.text: Prefer targets with unexplored acquisition channels, since they leave more growth for you.
principles.quote: The less acquisition channels the seller has explored, the better, as it’s more growth opportunities for you
